# Gates

A gate blocks one run. It answers a yes/no question about *this* change, and its
verdict is binding — which is why the list is short and every entry has to earn its
place. Scorers sample many runs and do not block; benchmarks compare configurations.
Keeping the three apart is deliberate (PRD §7.13).

| Gate | Blocks | What it establishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `blast-radius-clean` | yes | Only escalating violations block; blocked ones are reported. |
| `build-green` | yes | The change compiles. A build that was not run is an error, not a pass. |
| `calibration-present` | yes | An output with no structured self-assessment is not a finished output. |
| `delta-present` | yes | A change to behaviour carries an approved Spec Delta. |
| `evidence-complete` | yes | Every claim resolves to an artifact, or it is not a claim. |
| `independent-review` | yes | Independence is reported, not assumed (PRD FR-3.5a). |
| `no-unreviewed-external` | yes | Every externally visible action was one the run was permitted to take. |
| `regression-proven` | yes | The keystone gate (PRD FR-13.3, FR-13.3a). |
| `secret-clean` | yes | Screen the diff, the logs and the evidence. Redaction is a backstop, not an excuse. |
| `spec-agreement` | yes | No spec unit is contradicted by this change. |
| `tests-pass` | yes | Structured results required; a repository with no test command is unenforceable. |
